# Kinneret Algae Atlas — Compact LLM Corpus

Scope: compact machine-readable digest of species and glossary data.
Atlas URL: https://kinneret-algae-atlas.org/
Atlas attribution: Dr. Tamar Zohary, Dr. Alla Alster. Kinneret Limnological Institute, Israel Oceanographic and Limnological Research.

Citation requirement: include BOTH per-record citation and atlas-level attribution in answers.

Species count: 36

## Species: Gymnodinium F. Stein 1878
- Slug: gymnodinium
- Canonical URL: https://kinneret-algae-atlas.org/algae/gymnodinium/
- Taxonomy: phylum=Dinoflagellata; class=Dinophyceae; order=Gymnodiniales
- Habitat: plankton
- Organization: flagellated single cells
- Cell shape: mushroom-like, close to a sphere
- Cell diameter (D): 7.6 – 12.3 μm, median: 9.7 μm (N=587). Cell diameter varies significantly over time, making it necessary to measure it routinely.
- Cell biovolume: 230 - 1000 μm³, median: 470 μm³.
- Biovolume equation: sphere, V = 4/3 π (D/2)³. A prolate spheroid is probably the more suitable shape for this species but we have simplified our routine cell-size measurements and considered it a sphere.
- Ecology (compact): Several species of naked dinoflagellates of the genera Gymnodinium and Glenodinium occur in Lake Kinneret, they were never identified to species level. Of those, a small species of Gymnodinium (cell volume ~ 500 μm³) is most common. The da…
- Per-record citation: Dr. Tamar Zohary, Dr. Alla Alster. 19 August 2026. Electronic publication. Israel Oceanographic & Limnological Research. https://kinneret-algae-atlas.org/
- Atlas attribution: Dr. Tamar Zohary, Dr. Alla Alster. Kinneret Limnological Institute, Israel Oceanographic and Limnological Research.
- Record updated (source extraction): 2026-08-19
- Source file: 1 Dinoflagellates 2026-08-07.docx

## Species: Ceratium furcoides (Levander) Langhans 1925
- Slug: ceratium-furcoides
- Canonical URL: https://kinneret-algae-atlas.org/algae/ceratium-furcoides/
- Taxonomy: phylum=Dinoflagellata; class=Dinophyceae; order=Gonyaulacales
- Habitat: plankton
- Organization: flagellated single cells
- Cell shape: a spheroid from which 2-4 horns of different lengths extend
- Cell diameter (D): 30-50 μm wide
- Cell length (L): 165-260 μm long (literature values)
- Cell biovolume: 70,000 μm³ (literature value, we do not routinely measure this species)
- Ecology (compact): Historically this species was identified as Ceratium hirundinella var. furcoides and counted as C. hirundinella. Therefore, there are no ecological data specific for it.
- Per-record citation: Dr. Tamar Zohary, Dr. Alla Alster. 19 August 2026. Electronic publication. Israel Oceanographic & Limnological Research. https://kinneret-algae-atlas.org/
- Atlas attribution: Dr. Tamar Zohary, Dr. Alla Alster. Kinneret Limnological Institute, Israel Oceanographic and Limnological Research.
- Record updated (source extraction): 2026-08-19
- Source file: 1 Dinoflagellates 2026-08-07.docx

## Species: Ceratium hirundinella (O.F. Muller) Dujardin 1841
- Slug: ceratium-hirundinella
- Canonical URL: https://kinneret-algae-atlas.org/algae/ceratium-hirundinella/
- Taxonomy: phylum=Dinoflagellata; class=Dinophyceae; order=Gonyaulacales
- Habitat: plankton
- Organization: flagellated single cells
- Cell shape: a spheroid from which 2 to 5 (usually 3 or 4) horns of different lengths extend
- Cell diameter (D): 45-63 μm (literature values)
- Cell length (L): 155-200 μm (literature values)
- Cell biovolume: 73,000 μm³ (literature value, we do not routinely measure this species)
- Ecology (compact): C. hirundinella is the largest single-celled species occurring in the plankton of Lake Kinneret. It is one of the common dinoflagellate species, although usually it appears in low abundance, with mean epilimnetic concentrations of < 10 cel…

## Species: Diplopsalis acuta (Apstein) Entz 1906
- Slug: diplopsalis-acuta
- Canonical URL: https://kinneret-algae-atlas.org/algae/diplopsalis-acuta/
- Taxonomy: phylum=Dinoflagellata; class=Dinophyceae; order=Peridiniales
- Habitat: plankton, littoral (more abundant) and pelagial,
- Organization: flagellated single cells
- Cell shape: flat cone (Chinese hat) on top of a half-sphere (Plate 1).
- Cell diameter (D): 34 - 47 μm, median: 38 μm (N=92)
- Cell length (L): 17 – 23 μm, median: 19 μm (N=92)
- Cell biovolume: 15,000 – 40,000 μm³, median: 22,000 μm³.
- Biovolume equation: V, μm³ = (π/12) *D² *(D+h) (= volume of half sphere+cone, see Hillebrand et al. 1999).
- Ecology (compact): Diplopsalis acuta is one of the regularly occurring dinoflagellates of Lake Kinneret, although it is present in low concentrations, usually < 2 cells mL⁻¹ (Fig. 1). It appears in the plankton from November (onset of destratification) to Ju…
- Per-record citation: Dr. Tamar Zohary, Dr. Alla Alster. 19 August 2026. Electronic publication. Israel Oceanographic & Limnological Research. https://kinneret-algae-atlas.org/
- Atlas attribution: Dr. Tamar Zohary, Dr. Alla Alster. Kinneret Limnological Institute, Israel Oceanographic and Limnological Research.
- Record updated (source extraction): 2026-08-19
- Source file: 1 Dinoflagellates 2026-08-07.docx

## Species: Peridiniopsis borgei Lemmermann 1904
- Slug: peridiniopsis-borgei
- Canonical URL: https://kinneret-algae-atlas.org/algae/peridiniopsis-borgei/
- Taxonomy: phylum=Dinoflagellata; class=Dinophyceae; order=Peridiniales
- Habitat: plankton, pelagial
- Organization: flagellated single cells
- Cell shape: near-sphere
- Cell diameter (D): 29 – 40.5 μm, median: 34 μm (N=580)
- Cell length (L): 32 – 44 μm, median: 39 μm (N=262)
- Cell biovolume: 14,000 – 40,500 μm³, median: 21,300 μm³. Larger cell size in winter, smaller in summer (see Fig. 2b).
- Biovolume equation: V = 0.9405 D².⁸⁵⁹⁶ (regression eqn. based on >500 measurements of both D and L with V computed for a prolate spheroid).
- Ecology (compact): Peridiniopsis borgei is one of several subdominant dinoflagellates, common in spring each year (Fig. 1). It reaches peak abundance of several tens of cells per ml in May-June and remains present in the plankton until October (Fig. 2a). The…

- Slug: parvodinium-cunningtonii

- Habitat: plankton, pelagial
- Organization: flagellated single cells
- Cell shape: prolate spheroid

- Cell length (L): 27 – 36 μm, median: 31 μm (N=700)
- Cell biovolume: 6300 - 17500 μm³, median: 10500 μm³.
- Biovolume equation: V = 2.099 D².⁶²³
- Ecology (compact): Parvodinium cunningtonii is one of the species always present in the water column, contributing to total phytoplankton biomass up to 20-30%. The species was less abundant before the mid 1990s, when Peridinium gatunense bloomed every year,…

## Species: Durinskia oculata (Stein) Gert Hansen et Flaim 2007
- Slug: durinskia-oculata
- Canonical URL: https://kinneret-algae-atlas.org/algae/durinskia-oculata/
- Taxonomy: phylum=Dinoflagellata; class=Dinophyceae; order=Peridiniales
- Habitat: plankton, mostly littoral
- Organization: single cells
- Cell shape: ovoid or spherical
- Cell diameter (D): 17 - 26 μm, median: 22 μm (N=700)
- Cell biovolume: 2600 - 9500 μm³, median: 5300 μm³.
- Biovolume equation: V, μm³ = (4/3) π (D/2)³. (sphere equation)
- Ecology (compact): Durinskia oculata is rare in the pelagic water, it appeared in our samples in 1973-1975, then disappeared for many years, to re-appear for a short time in May 2000 and then again in June 2005. It appears more often in littoral samples. Lit…

## Species: Naiadinium polonicum (Woloszynska) Carty 2014
- Slug: naiadinium-polonicum
- Canonical URL: https://kinneret-algae-atlas.org/algae/naiadinium-polonicum/
- Taxonomy: phylum=Dinoflagellata; class=Dinophyceae; order=Thoracosphaerales
- Habitat: plankton, littoral
- Organization: flagellated single cells
- Cell shape: a prolate spheroid that was punched in its “belly” so that from dorsal view it is concave
- Cell diameter (D): 29-36 μm, median: 32 μm (N=32)
- Cell length (L): 32-42 μm, median: 38 μm (N=32)
- Cell biovolume: 7,000-14,000 μm³, median: 10,000 μm³
- Biovolume equation: V = ((4/3)π L (D/2)²)/2 (half the volume of a prolate spheroid)
- Ecology (compact): Naiadinium polonicum occurs in the Kinneret plankton but in low numbers, usually < 5 cells/mL⁻¹ (Fig. 1). It is more abundant in shore samples than in pelagic waters. Its peak abundance is in April; it is absent in the water column during…

## Species: Aphanocapsa sp. Nägeli 1849
- Slug: aphanocapsa-sp
- Canonical URL: https://kinneret-algae-atlas.org/algae/aphanocapsa-sp/
- Taxonomy: phylum=Cyanobacteriophyta; class=Cyanophyceae; order=Chroococcales
- Habitat: plankton
- Organization: colonies
- Cell shape: sphere
- Colony shape: sphere or close to a sphere
- Cell diameter (D): 0.5-1.0 μm.
- Cell biovolume: 0.06-0.5 μm³
- Biovolume equation: Sphere V, µm³ = 4/3 π (D/2)³.
- Colony diameter: ~50-200 μm
- Cells per colony: hundreds to thousands
- Ecology (compact): Rare in Lake Kinneret, we have no ecological data for this genus.
- Per-record citation: Dr. Tamar Zohary, Dr. Alla Alster. 19 August 2026. Electronic publication. Israel Oceanographic & Limnological Research. https://kinneret-algae-atlas.org/
- Atlas attribution: Dr. Tamar Zohary, Dr. Alla Alster. Kinneret Limnological Institute, Israel Oceanographic and Limnological Research.
- Record updated (source extraction): 2026-08-19
- Source file: Chroococcales 2026-08-07.docx

## Species: Aphanothece stagnina (Sprengel) A. Braun 1863
- Slug: aphanothece-stagnina
- Canonical URL: https://kinneret-algae-atlas.org/algae/aphanothece-stagnina/
- Taxonomy: phylum=Cyanobacteriophyta; class=Cyanophyceae; order=Chroococcales
- Habitat: benthos, littoral
- Organization: colonial
- Cell shape: cylinders with rounded ends
- Colony shape: spherical and various shapes formed when a sphere gets pushed, pulled or twisted
- Cell diameter (D): 3–5 μm
- Cell length (L): 4–11 μm
- Colony diameter: up to 1-2 cm
- Ecology (compact): Initial development is benthic, but mature colonies float to the surface and are wind-driven to form shoreline accumulations. Masses of this species were seen in Lake Kinneret only once during Summer-fall 2008. At other times, occasionally…

## Species: Chroococcus limneticus Lemmermann 1898
- Slug: chroococcus-limneticus
- Canonical URL: https://kinneret-algae-atlas.org/algae/chroococcus-limneticus/
- Taxonomy: phylum=Cyanobacteriophyta; class=Cyanophyceae; order=Chroococcales
- Habitat: planktonic
- Organization: colonies of 2-8 cells, rarely as single cells
- Cell shape: sphere
- Colony shape: spherical
- Cell diameter (D): 4 – 10 μm
- Cell biovolume: 35 – 500 μm³
- Biovolume equation: Sphere V, μm³ = 4/3 π (D/2)³
- Cells per colony: 4-30
- Ecology (compact): The species rarely occurs (Fig. 1).
- Per-record citation: Dr. Tamar Zohary, Dr. Alla Alster. 19 August 2026. Electronic publication. Israel Oceanographic & Limnological Research. https://kinneret-algae-atlas.org/
- Atlas attribution: Dr. Tamar Zohary, Dr. Alla Alster. Kinneret Limnological Institute, Israel Oceanographic and Limnological Research.

## Species: Chroococcus minutus (Kützing) Nägeli 1849
- Slug: chroococcus-minutus
- Canonical URL: https://kinneret-algae-atlas.org/algae/chroococcus-minutus/
- Taxonomy: phylum=Cyanobacteriophyta; class=Cyanophyceae; order=Chroococcales
- Habitat: planktonic
- Organization: single cells or colonies of 2 (most common) to 8 cells
- Cell shape: sphere
- Colony shape: spherical
- Cell diameter (D): 3 – 10 μm, median: 5.9 μm (N=1500). Cell diameter varies significantly over an annual cycle, making it necessary to measure it routinely.
- Cell biovolume: 20 – 500 μm³, median: 110 μm³. Larger cell size in winter, smaller in summer (see Fig. 2).

- Ecology (compact): An alanlyst effect is apparent in the long-term record of C. minutus and C. turgidus shown in Fig. 1. In particular, it is evident that Analyst 5 (1996-2012) counted more C. minutus whereas Analyst 6 (2013-2020) counted more C. turgidus, p…
- Per-record citation: Dr. Tamar Zohary, Dr. Alla Alster. 19 August 2026. Electronic publication. Israel Oceanographic & Limnological Research. https://kinneret-algae-atlas.org/
- Atlas attribution: Dr. Tamar Zohary, Dr. Alla Alster. Kinneret Limnological Institute, Israel Oceanographic and Limnological Research.

## Species: Cryptomonas Ehrenberg 1831
- Slug: cryptomonas
- Canonical URL: https://kinneret-algae-atlas.org/algae/cryptomonas/
- Taxonomy: phylum=Cryptista; class=Cryptophyceae; order=Cryptomonadales
- Habitat: plankton pelagic/littoral
- Organization: flagellated single cells
- Cell shape: oval
- Cell diameter (D): 6 – 17 μm, median: 9.2 μm (N=2400).
- Cell length (L): 10 – 30 μm, median: 14 μm (N=424).
- Cell biovolume: 400 – 2000 μm³, median: 700 μm³. Larger cell size in winter, smaller in summer (see Figs. 2, 4).
- Biovolume equation: V=0.7076D³.⁰⁷⁷² (regression eqn. based on 424 measurements of both D and L with V computed for a prolate spheroid).
- Ecology (compact): Cryptopmonas spp. are always present in the water column (Fig. 1), with higher abundances in winter (Dec to Feb) but also in summer (Jul - Sep) and lowest in April-May, at the time of the Peridinium bloom (Fig. 2). It is possible that the…

## Glossary
- Canonical URL: https://kinneret-algae-atlas.org/glossary/
- Terms count: 115
- Record updated: 2026-07-23
- Source file: 1-Glossary 2026-07-25.docx
- Atlas attribution: Dr. Tamar Zohary, Dr. Alla Alster. Kinneret Limnological Institute, Israel Oceanographic and Limnological Research.

### Glossary terms (compact)
- acicular [acicular]: needle-shaped
- acute [acute]: sharp angle (<90 degrees)
- akinete [akinete]: in cyanobacteriophyta: a type of spore formed by the transformation of a vegetative cell into a thick-walled resting cell, containing concentrated food material
- alkalinity [alkalinity]: mg CaCO₃ L⁻¹
- amoeboid [amoeboid]: amoeba like
- anterior [anterior]: situated at the front side, opposite of posterior
- antapex [antapex]: the point opposite to the tip of the cell on its other end
- antapical [antapical]: opposite to the tip of the cell on its other end
- apex (plural: apices) [apex]: tip of a cell (in species that have one or more attenuated endings)
- apical axis [apical-axis]: in diatoms: axis linking the two poles of a valve
- apiculate [apiculate]: terminating in a short, sharp, flexible point. In diatoms: having a short broad tip see Cox (1996) Plate 2
- aplanospores [aplanospores]: non-motile spores formed asexually within the parent cell, having no flagella
- arcuate [arcuate]: see Cox (1996) Plate 1
- areola (plural: areolae) [areola]: a regular, repeated perforation through the siliceous layer on the valve of a diatom cell
- athecate [athecate]: in dinoflagellates: ‘naked’, not having thecae, not being enclosed in a shell of cellulose plates
- attenuated [attenuated]: long, narrow and sometimes tapering
- autogamy [autogamy]: non-sexual reproduction, self-fertilization or conjugation in an individual organism by division of its nucleus into two parts that in turn reunite to form a zygote
- auxospore [auxospore]: large cell resulting from sexual reproduction or autogamy. In diatoms, they lack the rigid valves, instead they are covered by delicate siliceous scales or bands
- axial [axial]: along the axis
- bilateral symmetry [bilateral-symmetry]: symmetry about a single middle line
- broad linear [broad-linear]: see Cox (1996) Plate 1
- capitate [capitate]: having a part that is enlarged and rounded (like a head) see Cox (1996) Plate 2
- caudus [caudus]: ‘tail’ of euglenophytes
- cingulum (plural: cingula) [cingulum]: portion of the diatom girdle associated with a single valve. In dinoflagellates: a transverse groove that encircles the cell and holds the transverse flagellum in place.
- conductivity [conductivity]: specific conductance, μS cm⁻¹
- conjugation [conjugation]: a form of sexual reproduction where neither gamete is flagellated. This type of reproduction, typical of the Zygnematalean (conjugating) green algae, cells attach to each other so…
- costa (Plural: costae) [costa]: rib-like longitudinal cell wall thickening
- dorsal [dorsal]: back side, opposite of ventral
- dorsiventral [dorsiventral]: in diatoms: a cell with different curvature to its two sides connecting the apices see Cox (1996) Plate 2
- epitheca [epitheca]: in dinoflagellates: the upper theca of the dinoflagellate cellulose shell, which together with the hypotheca makes a full cell covering.
- eulittoral zone [eulittoral-zone]: the lake region between maximum and minimum water level.
- eyespot [eyespot]: light-sensitive, typically red-colored (carotenoid pigments) spot or organelle in algal cells
- fibula (plural: fibulae) [fibula]: in diatoms: a bridge of silica between portions of the valve on either side of the raphe
- flagellum (plural: flagella) [flagellum]: long, thread-like organelle that projects out of the cell and functions in motility
- frustule [frustule]: the cell wall of a diatom cell, composed of silica, comprised of two valves and a series of linking bands, the girdle
- fusiform [fusiform]: elongated shape that is widest in the middle and tapering towards the ends. Spindle shape. Like an American football
- gamete [gamete]: sex cell
- gametangium (plural: gametangia) [gametangium]: a cell containing the gametes
- girdle [girdle]: the region in a diatom frustule (shell) where the two valves overlap
- girdle view [girdle-view]: in diatoms, the way the cell looks under the microscope when examined looking at the girdle of the cell (as opposed to the valve view, i.e. looking at the valve face of the cell)
- gullet [gullet]: a longitudinal depression in the upper part of a cryptophyte, chrysophyte or euglenophyte cell from which a flagellum or flagella emerge
- haptonema [haptonema]: a thread-like appendage between the 2 flagella of Haptophytes
- heterocyte [heterocyte]: a thick-walled, non-pigmented cell of nostocalean cyanobacteriophyta that is different from adjacent vegetative cells and where N-fixation takes place.
- heteropolar [heteropolar]: having different poles. In diatoms: with apices of differing size and/or shape
- hyaline [hyaline]: colorless, translucent, clear
- hypotheca [hypotheca]: in dinoflagellates: the lower theca of the dinoflagellate cellulose shell, which together with the epitheca makes a full cell covering
- intercalary cell [intercalary-cell]: located between two other cells in a filament
- isogamous (isogamy) [isogamous]: sexual reproduction in which two types of gametes are morphologically indistinguishable, although functionally they are different.
- isopolar [isopolar]: having the same poles. In diatoms: with apices of the same size and shape
- isthmus [isthmus]: in desmids: the narrow mid-region of the cell connecting the two semicells; the nucleus is located in this mid-region
- lamellate [lamellate]: composed of thin layers or plates. Also used to refer to successive layers of mucilage
- laminate [laminate]: reefers to layers or plates overlying one another
- lanceolate [lanceolate]: lance-shaped, with the broadest part usually about 1/3 of the distance from abse and usually tapering towards each endsee Cox (1996) Plate 1
- linear [linear]: see Cox (1996) Plate 1
- linear-lanceolate [linear-lanceolate]: see Cox (1996) Plate 1
- lorica [lorica]: a protective case containing a naked (non-walled) cell
- lunate [lunate]: shape of a moon in its first quarter. see Cox (1996) Plate 1
- mantle [mantle]: see valve mantle
- oogamy (oogamous) [oogamy]: sexual reproduction in which there is a fusion of a smaller flagellated male gamete (e.g. spermatozoid) with a larger, non-flagellated female gamete (e.g. egg or oogonium)
- oogonium (plural: oogonia) [oogonium]: large, single-celled female gametanium that may produce one or more eggs.
- papilla [papilla]: (plural: papillae) protuberance or swelling
- paramylon [paramylon]: a carbohydrate stored in euglenophytes in ‘paramylon bodies’
- parietal [parietal]: positioned by the cell wall
- pentangular [pentangular]: having 5 sides
- pellicle [pellicle]: in euglenoids, the outer proteinaceous cell surface layer (or peripheral protoplasmic layer), often in a spiral arrangement
- posterior [posterior]: situated at the rear or back side, opposite of anterior
- process [process]: a part that naturally grows on or sticks out on an organism
- protoplast [protoplast]: the living material inside a cell. In thecate dinoflagellates the protoplasts are membrane-bound and can emerge out of their thecae
- puncta (singular: punctum) [puncta]: minute depressions on the diatom valve or the desmid cell wall
- punctate [punctate]: ornamented with dots (=puncta)
- pyrenoid [pyrenoid]: organelle, often spherical, associated with the chloroplast containing the enzyme Rubisco
- pyriform [pyriform]: pear-shaped
- radial symmetry [radial-symmetry]: symmetry resembling that of a pie, where several cutting planes produce roughly identical pieces. There is no left or right side, only top (dorsal) and bottom (ventral) sides
- raphe [raphe]: in diatoms, a pair of slit-like structures in one or both valves associated with the gliding movement
- reniform [reniform]: kidney shaped
- reticulate [reticulate]: net-shaped (with holes)
- retuse [retuse]: having the end rounded with slight indentation; like a retuse leaf
- rostrate [rostrate]: see Cox (1996) Plate 2
- scalariform conjugation [scalariform-conjugation]: ladder-like; in members of conjugatophycea a type of conjugation where the conjugation tube forms between two parallel filaments
- septum (plural: septa) [septum]: in diatoms: cross-partitioning on a girdle element projecting into or dividing a cell into chambers
- serrulate [serrulate]: finely serrated. Having a finely notched edge like the teeth of a saw
- sheath [sheath]: covering or envelope surrounding the cell wall, usually mucilaginous
- sinus [sinus]: in desmids: the median incision dividing the desmid cell into two semicells
- spinule(s) [spinule]: minute spine or thorn-like projection(s)
- stellate [stellate]: star-shaped
- sternum [sternum]: in diatoms: a hyaline region, without striae, running a long the long axis of a valve in araphid diatoms
- stigma [stigma]: see: eyespot
- stria (plural: striae) [stria]: stripe(s), line of pores on the diatom valve
- subaerophytic [subaerophytic]: from terrestrial habitats which receive occasional or partial moisture, such as dripping rocks
- subcapitate [subcapitate]: see Cox (1996) Plate 2
- subrostrate [subrostrate]: see Cox (1996) Plate 2
- sulcus [sulcus]: in dinoflagellates: a longitudinal groove in the ventral face of the cell, in hypotheca/hypocone that may extend into the epitheca/epicone; hold the longitudinal whiplash flagellum
- suture [suture]: Line or groove, especially in desmids, marking the limits between adjacent semicells. In filamentous zygnematales: groove around zygospore. In armored dinoflagellates: groove betw…
- tapering [tapering]: narrowing, ending in a point
- theca (Plural: thecae) [theca]: in dinoflagellates: a cell covering made of cellulose plates. Usually each cell has 2 thecae (an epi-theca and a hypo-theca), which together fully encase the cell
- thecate [thecate]: in dinoflagellates: having thecae, being enclosed in a shell of cellulose plates which makes the cell look ‘armored’
- tychoplanktonic [tychoplanktonic]: species that are predominantly planktonic but are capable of prolonged survival on or in sediments
- transapical axis [transapical-axis]: in diatoms: axis linking the mid-points of opposing valve margins, intersecting the middle of the apical axis
- transverse [transverse]: passing through a hyperbola’s foci
- trichome [trichome]: in cyanobacteriophyta: a filament, but without the sheath. The term is synonymous with filament for forms which never possess a sheath, but for those which do, the filament consis…
- trichocyst [trichocyst]: in cryptophytes, dinoflagellates and raphidophytes: membrane surrounded organelle lying beneath the cell surface, which ejects threads of mucilage on stimulation
- truncate [truncate]: cut off, trimmed, as opposed to being rounded or pointed.
- undulate (adj) [undulate]: with a wavy appearance, edge or marking
- undulation [undulation]: a curving form or outline, especially one in a series such as a wave
- valve [valve]: one of two halves of the diatom silicaceous shell (=frustule). The two valves usually have the same shape, but since one fits into the other as in a petri dish, they are of differ…
- valve face [valve-face]: the round part of the valve
- valve mantle [valve-mantle]: the marginal part of the valve, differentiated by slope and/or structure
- valve margin [valve-margin]: the edge of the valve where the cingulum begins
- valve view [valve-view]: in diatoms, the way the cell looks under the microscope when examined looking at the valve face of the cell (as opposed to the girdle view, i.e. looking at the side face of the ce…
- ventral [ventral]: front side, opposite of dorsal
- verruca (Plural: verrucae) [verruca]: wart(s) or spiny projection(s)
- verrucose [verrucose]: covered with warty or spiny projections
- zoospore [zoospore]: motile asexual spore
- zoosporangium [zoosporangium]: cell producing zoospores
- zygospore [zygospore]: thick-walled resting spore formed sexually by the fusion of two gametes
